newsitem.title: UK: Analysts' comments on sacking of Russia's Lebed.
newsitem.headline: Analysts' comments on sacking of Russia's Lebed.

text.p: Foreign investors said news on Thursday that Russian President Boris Yeltsin had sacked his security chief Alexander Lebed should come as no surprise to investors in so volatile a market.
KENT OSBAND, EMERGING MARKET STRATEGIST, HSBC

"The ruling establishment will effectively close ranks to prevent Lebed from mounting a successful coup. Though he is extremely popular with the people the Russian army is not prepared to mutiny. The showdown has been coming for a while."
"This is a festering sore whose gravity the market has not fully appreciated. The news can't help but wake people up to the fact that this is not your standard BB-rated country."
"We've seen a big sell off. I'd start purchasing here. We're going to fall a bit more but when the smoke clears the market will rally on this."
JEAN DE BOLLE, EMERGING MARKET STRATEGIST, FOREIGN & COLONIAL
"Given the number of things that can go wrong, it is not one of the worst outcomes."
"It's another symptom of the market's volatile nature."

"We have a positive long term view on Russia because we believe reform will continue but one has to recognise it is very risky. We would advise investors to have a small part of their portfolios in Russia but if they are taking a five-year view it still offers good value."
ALEX BEBOV, RUSSIA ANALYST, JP MORGAN
"I think Yeltsin showed clearly he will remain in control, he seemed very angry at the attempt to create a situation where elections were inevitable."
"The risk exists that Lebed will be able to create more noise. But he can do less now that he is outside the political establishment."

"As far as the political establishment is concerned he has very few allies in government. This is a solution to the Kulikov/Lebed crisis and Yeltsin showed fast enough that he's in control." --Caroline Brothers, London Newsroom +44 171 542 2734
